title: Kerri Colfer:
title_short: Kerri Colfer · Policy Keeps Our Communities Safe
headline: NIWRC’s Director of Policy and Research explains the part of safety nobody films: policy and advocacy are what create the conditions for a community to be safe, and October’s awareness campaigns run on that data.
story: Kerri Colfer is Tlingit and runs policy and research at NIWRC. She is the quiet lane of the organisation: the data behind the awareness campaigns and the policy asks behind the safety. The interview is short and she is precise, so this is a short, precise cut: hope, the data, the payoff.

Do not use her “Safety to me is not just the absence of violence” line (03:00 to 03:10). That sentence is the spine of Lucy Simpson’s cut (NIWRCOKCLucySafetyIsNotAbsence001). Kerri’s cut is about policy, not the definition of safety.

Loops: L1 “How does policy keep anyone safe?” opens at 0:00 and closes at 0:07 (“create the conditions necessary to keep our communities safe”). L2 “What does safe look like, then?” opens at 0:00 and closes in the BUTTON (“people are really able to thrive”). Stakes: the extent of violence against Native people, which the campaigns exist to show.
do: Open on her mid-sentence with the hook text on frame 1.
Keep it short. Three bites, one end card.
Use C1 as the main picture and C2 for one cutaway. Sound from C1 only.
Put the key words on screen as she says them.
Use only the files named here.
dont: No logo, name or fade at 0:00.
Do not use “Safety to me is not just the absence of violence”. It is Lucy’s cut.
Do not use Event 20 (Are You Happy block) or her “I hate being on camera” aside (C2 Event 10 00:44).
No stock footage, no charts, no numbers on screen.
No Tribal affiliation on the super. Name and title only.

client_note: Why this matters: NIWRC is mid-rebrand from “ending gender-based violence” to “advancing safety broadly”. Kerri is the person who turns that into policy. This cut shows the client’s own framing in the words of the person who does the work.
